definitions.gloss: to butt in; to interrupt; to interject
definitions.explanation: To insert a comment or opinion into someone else's conversation or discussion, often uninvited. Literally 'to insert one's mouth.'

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}が{話|はなし}に{口|くち}を{挟|はさ}んできた。
{会議中|かいぎちゅう}に{上司|じょうし}が{口|くち}を{挟|はさ}む{余地|よち}もなかった。
examples.english: During the meeting, there was no room for the boss to interject.

notes:
USAGE: {口|くち}を{挟|はさ}む usually carries a slightly negative nuance, suggesting the interruption was unwelcome or unsolicited. However, it can also be neutral depending on context.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- [topic]に{口|くち}を{挟|はさ}む (to butt into [a topic/conversation])

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {話|はなし}に{口|くち}を{挟|はさ}む: to interrupt a conversation
- {口|くち}を{挟|はさ}む{余地|よち}がない: no room to get a word in
- {横|よこ}から{口|くち}を{挟|はさ}む: to butt in from the side

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口出|くちだ}しする: to meddle, to interfere (stronger negative nuance)
- {割|わ}り{込|こ}む: to cut in, to interrupt (more physical sense)
